source_evidence: BDCs are a type of closed-end investment fund. One way that BDCs can differ is in whether their shares are traded on national securities exchanges.
answer: A business development company (BDC) is a type of closed-end investment fund that gives retail investors a way to invest in small and medium-sized private companies, and to a lesser extent, other investments such as public companies. BDC shares are not all alike in how they trade: some BDCs have shares traded on national securities exchanges. BDCs can also use more debt and other leverage than many other types of funds, so their risks and structure can vary. Before considering a BDC, review its available information, investment strategy, fees, and risks.
